$comment: godot-game-factory's task format, GameTask (game-task/1: Godot 4.7, metres, Y up): one task a game ships with, on its orphan tasks branch (Tasks/<name>.json) and, split into the agent's and the grader's parts, in its dataset. The deterministic `probe` check kind is described for task authors in docs/task-probes.md, and every task is seeded; a build check's `fails_at_start` marks a start whose scripts don't load. tools/validate-game.py checks every task in a game repo's tasks branch and in a dataset against this schema and the rules it cannot express. A task play may send touches (`tap`, `drag`: a finger down at a point of the screen or a widget's centre, held, moved, several fingers at once), and a probe may read what the renderer drew (`render`: draw calls, triangles, texture memory). A task play may also stage a contact (`pin`, `damage`, `set`); an object select may leave the player out (`player` false); a probe may read the game's lowest time scale, whether it went on and its pause (`world`), and an object's short stops and the damage a staged hit did (`frozen`, `damage_taken`). An audio measure may read the sounds that start (`started_audible`, `sounds`, `repeats`) and select by a place (`near`). A task play may name the task plays that run before it on the same side (`after`), for a play that reads what another saves. An object or a component may be read for the light it gives off (`lit`, `glow`), and a select may ask for a part that is lit (`has.lit`). A probe may read text from a named shot of its own task play by the visual checks' model (`seen`: `shot`, a name or a list of 2 to 4, `rect`, `read` text, number or clock, `match`, `agg`; Lab game grader 1.13.0): it is a visual check, counted and switched with the judges. A widget click may be `optional`: a click on a control a game shows only in some states, no miss when nothing on screen matches it (a matched control that takes no press still is). A widget click, and a touch on a widget, may name a button by its caption exactly as the screen shows it, in any language, spaces and punctuation included (matched as written first, then alike ignoring case, spaces and punctuation). A widget click may be `disabled`: a click on a button the game disables by design, landed when that button is shown but disabled (without the mark, that is a miss). A widget click, and a tap on a widget, whose control only its own scroll areas hide scrolls them to it and presses in the next frame; one hidden any other way, and a drag's, presses nothing and is a miss that neither mark excuses. A click or a tap on a control something else is over presses nothing and is a miss that neither mark excuses (`covered by another control`); the widgets field `covered` says whether that is so. A sampled measure may say `since` (an event: its window and at count from the first sample whose reading meets the event's expect), and a `shot` input `when` (taken in the first frame its event comes). A task play may say `fresh`: it starts with the game's saved data cleared, as every play without `after` does, and never has `after`. A task play lasts up to 1200 s, and every time in one goes up to that (Lab game grader 1.18.0). A widget click no control takes is made on its text as shown, when exactly one place on screen reads it.

AtCamera.description: The player's camera, `forward` m along its view.
AtCamera.title: AtCamera

AtXYZ.description: A fixed point in the world (m).
AtXYZ.title: AtXYZ

AudioMeasure.description:
What the player hears (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.16): the AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D and
AudioStreamPlayer3D nodes playing that `select` matches, each at its volume at the listener (its own volume
times, for a placed one, its attenuation at the listener's distance; bus volumes left out): `count` (how
many), `audible` (how many at 0.001, -60 dB, or louder), `volume` (their sum), `max_volume` (the loudest);
`level` (the RMS of the Master bus's mixed output since the previous sample, buses and effects included);
`started` (how many matching players were found playing that weren't the frame before, in each sample's
interval; summed over the samples picked by default); and the sounds that start, every one however short, each
`play()` of a player watched every frame: `started_audible` (how many started audible at the listener in each
sample's interval: at 0.001 or louder with their bus's gain, no bus on their way muted; summed by default), and
from the names of the streams that started, in the order they started, over the samples picked: `sounds` (how many
different streams), `repeats` (how many started with the same stream as the start just before them). `sounds` and
`repeats` read nothing when a stream that started has no name of its own sound (one made in code, or one that
picks or mixes other streams: a randomizer, a polyphonic stream); they take no `agg`.
A play with an audio measure runs paced to real time; no play is heard. The volumes' and the level's threshold
is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
AudioMeasure.title: AudioMeasure

AudioSelect.description:
The players playing (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.16): by their stream's name (`sound`, a wildcard on the
stream resource's name: its file's name without the extension), the bus they play on (`sound_class`, a
wildcard on the bus's name), an owner the `owner` select matches (the player is that node or under it), and `near` a point (a placed
player, 2D or 3D, within the radius: where it plays, or for the started fields where it started; a player with no
place is near nothing, and a point that doesn't resolve leaves no value); none: every player playing.
AudioSelect.title: AudioSelect

Axis.description:
An axis event (<Mouse>/delta/x, <Gamepad>/leftStick/x) with its value, e.g. mouse look; <Mouse>/delta/* is
one mouse movement and <Mouse>/scroll/* so many notches of the wheel, any other axis keeps its value until
set again.
Axis.title: Axis

Boot.description:
The game starts (run from the project at the play's frame size, on a desktop of its own) and runs
`seconds` with no crash and no fatal error in its log.
Boot.title: Boot

Build.description:
The project imports and every script loads, with no script error in the engine's log.
`fails_at_start`: the task's start doesn't (a script that doesn't parse), and making it load is the task;
the start is never played, so nothing in the task may need it played (docs/task-probes.md, section
3.1; tools/validate-game.py).
Build.title: Build

Calibrate.description: Threshold s + f * (r - s): the start (s) and the developers' fix (r) measured in the grading environment.
Calibrate.title: Calibrate

Click.description:
A click on the first visible Control that takes one (not disabled) whose name (a wildcard) or class
matches, else the first button whose shown caption reads it, as a player's click presses it: the mouse at its
centre, the left button down and up. A caption is matched as written first (exactly as the screen shows it, in any
script, spaces and punctuation included), then in lower case with every run of other characters one `_`.
`optional`: a click on what a game shows only sometimes (a confirmation it asks only when a save exists): when no
shown Control matches it, the play goes on and the click is no input that missed; one that matches but takes no
press is still a miss. `disabled`: a click on a button the game disables by design (a locked choice): it has
landed when that button is shown disabled, and does nothing, as a player's click on it; without it, that is a miss.
A Control that only its own ScrollContainers hide (its centre out of their view, at any depth) is scrolled into
view first, the least way, as a player scrolls a list to it, and clicked in the next frame; one hidden any other way
(outside a Control that only clips, still out of view once scrolled) is not pressed and the click is a miss whatever
its marks. A Control something else is over, where a player's press at its centre would go to that instead (another
Control, a higher canvas layer, a dialog or a popup), is not pressed either: a miss whatever its marks.
A click no Control takes is made on its text as shown (Lab game grader 1.18.0): the one place on screen whose text
reads it (compared as a caption is: a Label's, any Control's own, a Label3D's, or texts side by side on one line
read joined), the mouse moved there and the left button down the next frame and up 0.1 s later; text shown in two
places or more is a miss.
Click.title: Click

CodeJudge.description:
A code reviewer's question over the run's own change (its diff from the start, text files) beside the game's
real change for the same problem (the seed's `reference`, a bug's fix from the game's history), which the agent
never sees.
CodeJudge.title: CodeJudge

ComponentSelect.description:
Nodes of a class (`component`: GPUParticles3D, AudioStreamPlayer3D, MeshInstance3D, Light3D, a game's own
script; the classes it inherits match), optionally under a node the `owner` select matches, by its name
(`name`, a wildcard), near a point, of a mesh (`mesh`, a wildcard on its mesh resource's name), and
`visible`: only those shown (as the `visible` field reads them); `effect`: only live particle effects (a
GPUParticles or CPUParticles node, 3D or 2D, that is emitting), with or without `component`; `inactive`:
hidden nodes too, else only those that are shown (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.5).
ComponentSelect.title: ComponentSelect

ComponentsMeasure.description:
Nodes of a class, the parts of the scene (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.5): `x`, `y`, `z` and `speed` (m/s:
its own velocity, a CharacterBody's or a RigidBody's, when it isn't zero, else how far it moved since the
previous sample); `extent_x|y|z` (the world-aligned half-size of what it draws or collides with);
`simulating` (a rigid body that isn't frozen, or a collision shape of one); `intensity` and `on` (a light's
energy; it lights the scene: shown, of an energy above 0); `active` (shown and doing what it does: particles
emitting, a sound or an animation playing, a collision shape on, a light on) and `visible` (shown); `spin`
(deg/s: how fast it turns in the world, from its rotation every frame; docs/task-probes.md, section 2.5);
`world_yaw` and `world_pitch` (degrees in (-180, 180]: its own rotation in the world, angles like `yaw`, so
`to_angle` and `to_axis` apply; objects' `world_yaw:<Part>` for a node selected by where or what it is rather
than by a name); `prop:<path>` (a property of the node or a variable of its script; strings through
`match`). `intensity`, `extent_*` and `spin` depend on what a build chose, so their threshold is calibrated
or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
ComponentsMeasure.title: ComponentsMeasure

Cursor.description:
The mouse moved to a point of the frame (fractions 0-1, y down from the top); a following
<Mouse>/leftButton press and release clicks there.
Cursor.title: Cursor

Damage.description:
`damage` points dealt through the game's own damage method, `take_damage(amount, source)`, on the object `to`
selects nearest to the player (`{"player": true}`: the player): the node itself, else the first node below it
that has the method. `source` is the object `from` selects nearest to the one struck (default: the player, or,
when the player is struck, the nearest other node that has a `take_damage`). What the method returned is the
object's `damage_taken`: the damage actually applied, in a game under the factory's combat rule. No target, or
one without the method, is a miss the play reports (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.4).
Damage.title: Damage

Drag.description:
A finger put down at the first spot of `drag`, moved through the others evenly over `over` seconds (at once
without it), kept at the last for `hold` seconds, then lifted: a swipe, a slider, a virtual stick pushed over and
held there. `finger` as a tap's; two drags of different fingers at the same time are a pinch. One finger's touches
are at least 0.1 s apart, from one's lift to the next one's start. A drag with a spot whose widget isn't on screen
is a miss the play reports.
Drag.title: Drag

DrawnMeasure.description:
What is drawn in a place, whatever draws it (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.19): every 3D part drawn in the game
whose world box reaches the place (the box around `near`'s sphere, cut to its height band; or the square tube of
`radius` around a `line`), drawn alone by the probe's own cameras in the game's 3D world (else no value: a play
that draws nothing, a 2D game). Near a point: `drawn` (1 when anything is), `motion` (the share of what is drawn
there that changed since the previous sample: a moving mesh, particles, a panned material), `base_r|g|b` (the
mean drawn base colour, linear 0-1) and `base_change` (that colour's distance from the first sample's). Along a
line: `drawn`, `reach` (m from `from` to the furthest point drawn on it) and `length` (m of it drawn). Every field
but `drawn` depends on what a build drew, so its threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a
literal (tools/validate-game.py).
DrawnMeasure.title: DrawnMeasure

Event.description:
A moment of the play that its reading decides: the first sample (a measure's `since`) or the first frame (a
shot's `when`) at which `measure`, read as one sample (no window, at, agg or since of its own), meets `expect`, a
literal threshold. `within`: it counts only that many seconds from the play's start (`since`) or from the shot's `t`
(`when`); else to the play's end. A measure's `since` counts its `window` and `at` from that moment, and reads
nothing when it never comes; a shot's `when` that never comes is a missed input (docs/task-probes.md).
Event.title: Event

FileExists.description: At least `min_count` project files match `glob` (relative to the project; e.g. scenes/*.tscn).
FileExists.title: FileExists

GroundMeasure.description:
The ground (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.17): where a ray straight down meets a physics body's shape first
(areas and the player's aside; with `select`, only shapes of objects it matches or of the nodes below them
count), at a point `xz` [x, z] (`height`, y in m; `hit`, 1 when it met anything) or over a box `box` [x0, z0, x1,
z1] sampled on a `grid` x `grid` lattice (`min`, `max`, `mean` of the heights, `range` = max - min, the relief;
`hits`). `range`'s threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
GroundMeasure.title: GroundMeasure

Has.description:
A part the object carries (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.4): it matches when the node itself or a node
below it matches every key given: `component` (its class, as a select names one), `lit` (it gives off light, as the components `lit`
field reads it), `visible` (a node that
draws and is shown), `near` (the part's own place within `radius` m of a point), `simulating` (a
RigidBody3D or RigidBody2D that isn't frozen, or a collision shape of one): an object a player can shove
(docs/task-probes.md, section 2.4).
Has.title: Has

Judge.description:
The game judge's question over evidence the grader takes itself (screenshots and gameplay frames of a scripted
play, and the brief), item by item; never the agent's own words. `before`: the grader also plays the game as it
was at the start, and the judge compares (a seeded task that changes how the game looks or plays). `route`: a
project file in which the agent leaves inputs that play its game through (the probe's [{t, key, press}] with
control paths, e.g. Tests/win_route.json); the grader plays it in its own clean copy as one more play, and the judge is told when
the file is missing or isn't a route. `plays`: the task's own scripted plays the screenshots are taken in (a
probe's TaskPlay: its scene, args and inputs), instead of the grader's idle look and its drive, which every task
shares and which never press a task's own keys or leave a game's title screen; each is played on every side the
check shows (the developer's game, the start on a `before` check, the reference on a `reference` check). `shots`:
how many screenshots of each of its plays it is shown (5 unless said), spread evenly over the play, so a short play
with many is a run of frames a quarter of a second apart in which motion shows (an ease or a cut, feet that slide, a
trail); its plays times its shots are a judge's 20 at most.
Judge.title: Judge

Key.description:
A key pressed or released, by its control path on <Keyboard>, <Mouse> or <Gamepad> (<Keyboard>/w,
<Keyboard>/space, <Mouse>/leftButton, <Gamepad>/buttonSouth). In a mobile game's play <Keyboard>/escape is the
phone's back button.
Key.title: Key

Line.description: A segment from `from` to `to` (points), and how far from it (`radius`, m) counts as on it.
Line.title: Line

LogAbsent.description: No line of the game's log during a boot matches `pattern` (a regular expression).
LogAbsent.title: LogAbsent

LogMeasure.description: Lines of the play's log matching `pattern`.
LogMeasure.title: LogMeasure

Move.description:
The mouse moved by `move` [dx, dy] pixels (right, down), spread evenly over `over` seconds (at once without it):
one mouse motion a frame, each the part due by then, as a mouse look reads it (`relative`); the cursor stays
where it is. To put the cursor on a point, use a cursor input.
Move.title: Move

Near.description:
Within `radius` m of `point`; `y_min`/`y_max` (m) also keep it within a height band: world y, or offsets from
the point's y with `y_relative` (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.13).
Near.title: Near

OnWidget.description:
The centre of the first visible widget of that name (a wildcard) or type, whatever its kind: a Control node (a
button, a stick, a panel), as a widgets select finds one; else of the first button whose caption reads it, as a
click's (exactly as shown first, in any script). A tap's widget that only its own ScrollContainers hide is
scrolled into view first and tapped in the next frame, and one something else is over is a miss, as for a click; a
drag's widget is taken as it is, and one scrolled out of its container's view is no spot: the touch is a miss.
OnWidget.title: OnWidget

Package.description:
The game's release export builds (its Windows Desktop preset, as a release would), and the exported game
boots.
Package.title: Package

PieceSelect.description:
Placed mesh pieces (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.14): of nodes of a class (MeshInstance3D,
MultiMeshInstance3D, GridMap, GeometryInstance3D, a game's own script; default every one), optionally by the
node's name, their mesh's name (`mesh`, a wildcard), an owner object the `owner` select matches, and near a
point (each piece by its own place).
PieceSelect.title: PieceSelect

PiecesMeasure.description:
Placed mesh pieces, whatever their form (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.14): a MeshInstance3D whose mesh has
triangles is one, each instance of a MultiMeshInstance3D one, each GridMap cell whose item has a mesh one, a
farther level of detail none; counted over all of them, never cut at the rows cap. `triangles`/
`visible_triangles`: the triangles those pieces (those drawn) hold; they depend on the meshes a build chose, so
their threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a literal (tools/validate-game.py).
PiecesMeasure.title: PiecesMeasure

Pin.description:
The object `pin` selects nearest to the player (never the player itself) held at its place for `hold` seconds
of play, put back before and after every frame's game logic with its velocity stilled while its own scripts run
on (it still turns, swings, blocks); with `front`, first set that many m ahead of the player along the way the
player faces (plus `offset`, m), at its own height, turned to face the player: a target or an opponent where
the player's blow or shot lands, whatever place a build gave it; with `at`, first set at that point (plus
`offset`), facing the player. A pin no object matches, or whose point doesn't resolve, is a miss the play
reports (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.4).
Pin.title: Pin

Probe.description:
A deterministic check (docs/task-probes.md): `measure` taken where `play` says, reduced to one number, compared with
`expect`. `describe` is the assertion in plain English, shown in the grade.
Probe.title: Probe

RenderMeasure.description:
What the renderer drew (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.20): `draw_calls` and `triangles`, the engine's own counts of
a frame (the 3D scene, its shadow passes and the 2D canvas, the UI's draws among them), the highest over the frames
since the previous sample; `texture_mb`, the texture memory in use at the sample (MiB). A budget's readings: a
literal threshold is allowed, since a budget is a number of its own (a mobile game's 700 draw calls).
RenderMeasure.title: RenderMeasure

SceneLoad.description:
At `t` the play changes to another scene of the project, as the game's own change of scene does; the play's
clock stands still while it changes (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1). With shots and teleports, one launch
visits several places and pictures each.
SceneLoad.title: SceneLoad

ScreenMeasure.description:
The frame the player sees (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.15): mean luminance of the frame as displayed, UI
included (keep the rect off the HUD), over `rect` [x0, y0, x1, y1] in fractions of the frame, y down (default
the whole frame). It moves between machines, so its threshold is calibrated or relative to the start, never a
literal (tools/validate-game.py).
ScreenMeasure.title: ScreenMeasure

Seed.description:
Where a seeded task starts: one of the studio's games at `commit`. `game` is its slug: the game's repository
(godot-game-<slug>) and its folder under the machine's games root.
`reference`: a later commit of that game whose change solves the task (a bug's fix), for calibrated probes, the code judge and the task check.
`history`: which history the two commits are from: "private", the game's own repository (its clone,
GitHub, a mirror), or "dataset", the rewritten history a Dataset.zip delivers (History/), whose
commit ids differ; the game's commit map translates either way.
Seed.title: Seed

SeenMeasure.description:
Text read from a named screenshot of the check's own task play by the visual checks' model (docs/task-probes.md,
section 2.22): the `shot` (a `shot` input of the play), cropped to
`rect` [x0, y0, x1, y1] in frame fractions (default the whole frame) and scaled up, is transcribed by the model
with one fixed prompt that says nothing of the task, each crop 3 times, the value the one 2 of 3 readings give.
`read`: `text` (1 when `match`, a regular expression, is found in what was read, else 0), `number` (the first
number read, as a ui number) or `clock` (the first time read, as a ui clock). For text no node gives (drawn by a
script, a shader or a texture); a node's text is read with `ui` or `widgets`. A visual check: it goes with the
judges wherever checks are switched or counted (VISUAL_CHECKS in an exported folder). `shot` may list 2 to 4
shots of the play with `read` number or clock and an `agg` (first, last, delta, rises, falls, min, max): each
read alone, then reduced in their order.
SeenMeasure.title: SeenMeasure

Select.description:
Nodes that match every key given: `component` (the node's own class: an engine class or one it inherits,
its script's class_name, or its script's file name without the extension), `tag` (a group it is in),
`name` (a wildcard on its name), `near` (within `radius` m of a point), `player` (true: the player; false: anything but the
player), `has` (a
part it carries that matches every key given there: a node with a drawn mesh near a point, one with a
rigid body), `where` (properties of the node compared with values: every one must hold), `inactive`
(hidden nodes match too; without it only nodes that are shown do).
Select.title: Select

SetProp.description:
A property (the path a prop: field reads, no array index) written on the object `on` selects nearest to the
player, or on every match with `all`: a number or a boolean onto a number or a boolean, a string onto a string;
for a property the task's start already has (a foe's health at 1, so one blow fells it through the game's own
death; the player's own high, so a staged fight can't end the play). A set no object or no property takes is a
miss the play reports (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.4).
SetProp.title: SetProp

Shot.description:
A screenshot at `t` with the UI, as the player sees it, named `shot` (shot_<name>.png beside the evenly spaced
ones): the grader's own picture of a moment, for a judge and for whoever reviews a run (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
Never a pass or fail by itself. `when`: taken in the first frame at or after `t` at which its event comes; a missed
input (kind shot_when) when it doesn't come in time.
Shot.title: Shot

StartPlus.description: Threshold s + d: the start (s) measured in the grading environment (a task with no developers' fix).
StartPlus.title: StartPlus

StartTimes.description: Threshold s * f: the start (s) measured in the grading environment (a task with no developers' fix).
StartTimes.title: StartTimes

Tap.description:
A finger put down at `tap` (a viewport point in fractions, y down from the top, or `{"widget": name}`: that
widget's centre) and lifted: the next frame, or after `hold` seconds (a long press, a button held). `finger`: which
finger (0-9, 0 unless said); taps and drags of different fingers may overlap in time (two thumbs). A tap whose
widget isn't on screen is a miss the play reports.
Tap.title: Tap

TaskPlay.description:
A task-defined scripted play: `inputs` (keys, axes, widget clicks, cursor moves, teleports, waits, touches, the stages of a contact)
sent at their times during `seconds`; its own `scene` instead of the task's play_scene (null: the project's
main scene) and `args` on its command line instead of the task's play_args (a flag, -name, then its values,
but never the grader's own: the engine flags in docs/task-probes.md section 1.1, -taskProbe*), each only when
the play has the key; and samples every `every` seconds (default 0.5).
`after`: the task plays (probe or judge plays of the task) that run and end on the same side before it starts,
for a play that reads what another writes (a save); one that failed still counts as run. It starts on the saved data
those plays and the plays they name left, and on nothing else's; every other play starts clean.
`fresh`: the play starts with the game's save state cleared, which every play without `after` already does; it says
so, and is never given with `after`.
TaskPlay.title: TaskPlay

Teleport.description:
The player placed at `teleport` (m) facing `yaw`: the grader's own way to reach a test spot; `hold`: for that
many seconds of play the player is put back there after every frame's game logic, for a game that sets its
player's place every frame (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
Teleport.title: Teleport

TeleportTo.description:
The player placed next to the object `teleport_to` selects nearest to it (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1): `distance` m from
it on the player's side, level with it, plus `offset` (m), facing `face` (a point) or else that object; for a spot
a build chose itself (an ore it placed). Nothing happens when no object matches. `hold`: as a teleport's, the
player kept at that spot for that many seconds of play (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
TeleportTo.title: TeleportTo

UiMeasure.description:
What the UI shows on screen (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18): the elements on screen at each sample, one
for each thing a drawn Control draws (its text, its picture, its box), only what is drawn (a hidden,
transparent or clipped-away Control is not; text in the 3D scene is not UI). `count` (one per element),
`text` (with `match`), `x`, `y`, `w`, `h` (its rectangle in fractions of the frame, y down); `of` combines the
elements `select` picks. `signature`: one value a sample for everything the select picks (kinds, texts,
rectangles), read with `agg` `changes` (how many samples show something other than the one before: a readout
that updates), `any`, `all` or `count` (samples showing anything); `of` is ignored (docs/task-probes.md,
section 2.18). `number`: the first number its text elements show, in reading order; `clock`: the first time
they show (h:mm:ss, m:ss, or else a number, as seconds); read with `rises`, `falls`, `changes` or `range` for
which way it moved, `of` ignored (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18). The way to check what a HUD shows.
UiMeasure.title: UiMeasure

UiSelect.description:
Which of the UI elements on screen (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.18): `kind` (text, box, image), `text` (a
regular expression the element's text must match; text elements only) and `rect` [x0, y0, x1, y1] in
fractions of the frame, y down from the top (the element's centre inside); none: every element on screen.
UiSelect.title: UiSelect

Value.description: A literal threshold, for facts that don't depend on the scene (counts, booleans).
Value.title: Value

View.description:
At `t` the player turns to the yaw and the camera to `view` [pitch, yaw] in degrees (pitch -89 to 89, a
positive one looks up), for a shot that faces a given way (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
View.title: View

Wait.description:
At `t` the play's clock holds for `wait` seconds of real time while the game runs on, paced to real time (each
frame waits for the wall clock to catch up with the game's own time), for what runs on the wall clock (a menu that
pages on real time). No samples, inputs or screenshots meanwhile; then the play goes on from `t` (docs/task-probes.md, section 1.1).
Wait.title: Wait

Where.description:
A property of the node (the path a prop: field reads) compared with a value: a number, a boolean (1
or 0) or a string; a node whose property doesn't resolve doesn't match.
Where.title: Where

WidgetSelect.description:
Widgets: the Control nodes of the game's window on screen, by their class (`component`: Button, Label,
ProgressBar, TextureRect, a game's own script) and/or name (a wildcard on the node's name); `text`: a regular
expression the widget's text must match. On screen is what the `visible` field reads 1 for: never a hidden or
transparent one, one under such a parent, one outside the frame or wholly clipped away. `visible` false keeps
the hidden ones too (the widget exists, shown or not); true is the default. A measure of the `visible` field
whose select doesn't say takes them too (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.6).
WidgetSelect.title: WidgetSelect

WorldMeasure.description:
The game as a whole (docs/task-probes.md, section 2.21), each the lowest over the frames since the previous
sample: `time_scale`, the engine's `Engine.time_scale` (time slowed, however briefly: 1 when it ran at its pace);
`flow`, how the game went on: 0 in a frame the tree was paused, else `Engine.time_scale` (a hit stop, whether a
build slows the game, stops its time or pauses the tree); and `paused`, 1 when the game was paused in any of those
frames ("Escape pauses the game").
WorldMeasure.title: WorldMeasure

play_args.description:
The game's command-line arguments for every play of the task (-scenario 2: ["-scenario", "2"]; they follow
`--` on the engine's command line); never the grader's own flags (TaskPlay).
play_args.title: Play Args

play_scene.description: The scene every play of the task opens (null: the project's main scene).
play_scene.title: Play Scene

player.description:
The player object for every play of the task (CameraMeasure, PlayerMeasure, `player` points and selects),
when the default finds the wrong one.
